input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed beige 'NO WHISKY, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, rocks glass, lettering, logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is on the TV screen at the right: a football match continues as a distant wide broadcast view of a bright green pitch, where tiny soft-focus players run naturally across the field; the TV screen shows no text, no score, no logos and no faces, only the distant pitch and tiny players. The TV set itself does not move. Everything else, including the sofa, the scarf, the coffee table with the whisky and deli food, the rug, the football on the floor, the floor lamp, the shelf with bottles, the plants, the bed and the poster, is completely still and motionless. Bright, warm, cozy night in a small tidy Japanese 8-tatami one-room apartment, interior magazine photography quality. No steam, no smoke, no haze.
